title: Apollo 1 pad fire
what: During a plugs-out test the cabin was pressurized with 100% oxygen. A flash fire spread so quickly there was no time to open the hatches; the crew died from carbon monoxide and toxic gases. The three-piece hatch took 90 s to open under ideal conditions and could not be opened under the fire's overpressure.
lesson: Oxygen-rich atmospheres turn ordinary materials into fast fuels. Material selection, cabin atmosphere and egress design must be driven by flammability data.

title: Apollo 13 oxygen tank explosion
what: Heater thermostatic switches were not modified for a higher ground voltage. On the pad the heaters overheated (~1000 F), degrading Teflon wire insulation inside oxygen tank 2, which later failed in flight and damaged tank 1.
lesson: Ignition of polymers inside high-pressure oxygen is a materials-flammability problem: it depends on oxygen concentration, pressure and the material.

title: Fire aboard space station Mir
what: A solid-fuel oxygen generator canister in Kvant-1 ignited, shooting a ~1 m flame that blocked access to one Soyuz and filled the modules with dense smoke. The crew used masks and foam extinguishers; the flame finally extinguished itself and life support cleared the smoke over several hours.
lesson: Smoke spreads through the whole vehicle, detection must be fast, and suppression in confined microgravity spaces is hard to aim.

title: Artemis II smoke alarm
what: A smoke alarm sounded aboard Orion about 80,000 miles from Earth. The commander noted it is the fastest way to get the crew's attention.
lesson: Beyond low Earth orbit there is no quick return: detectors must be reliable and resistant to nuisance alarms (dust vs smoke).
